summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Marisol Health through the model catalog UI and API, discussed performance benchmarks, model compatibility across quantizations and hardware, and next steps toward a POC.
transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-03-31 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42 min | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Sofia Martinez (CTO - Marisol), Liam O'Connor (Head of ML), Aisha Khan (Platform Engineer)

00:00 Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we did a quick calendar check, this is the model catalog walkthrough, we'll show the API, console and Optimize recommendations. I think Priya will drive most of the tech.
00:14 Priya Raman: Yup, hi all, quick agenda, 1) show model selection in the catalog, 2) look at benchmark comparisons, 3) compatibility matrix for quant/arch, 4) Q&A and next steps.
00:30 Sofia Martinez: Great, we have about 40 minutes, want to focus on latency and cost and how we can use open models in production.
00:42 Liam O'Connor: Also interested in quantization impacts and if Redwood supports int8/int4 or binary quant, and how that maps to our GPUs.
00:55 Priya Raman: Absolutely, we'll cover quant profiles, we support per-model quant presets and we surface recommendation in Optimize. Note: we sometimes refer to 'kv cache' but the auto-transcript may show 'kayvee cache' in the notes.
01:10 Priya Raman: (shares screen) here's the catalog, you can filter by size, family, license, and we have performance badges from our benchmarks: latency p50/p95, throughput, and token cost.
01:32 Jordan Lee: Quick qualifier — are you using hosted SaaS models today or self-hosting?
01:38 Aisha Khan: We run models in our VPC on GCP, a mix of hosted for prototypes and private for prod. Security is key — SSO, KMS, audit logs.
01:50 Jordan Lee: Ok, good. Redwood Dedicated or Private would map to that — we can do private control plane + customer VPC, bring-your-own-KMS, and provide audit logs. We'll share SOC2 and ISO docs.
02:05 Liam O'Connor: On benchmarks — do you run the same workloads that we have? Our seq lengths are typically 512-1024 tokens, conversational with some long-form outputs.
02:20 Priya Raman: We have benchmark buckets by seq len; note our latency charts are labeled p50/p95 for 128/512/1024. For example, on an A100 pool, a 7B model quantized to int8 shows ~60ms p50 at 512 tokens, p95 around 180ms under similar batching.
02:45 Sofia Martinez: That sounds promising; cost per token numbers?
02:52 Priya Raman: We show token unit estimates — each model has a 'unit cost' estimate that considers kernel efficiency and batching. Optimize will give suggestions: e.g., use int8 for throughput, or switch to a trimmed 3B for cheap assistant flows.
03:12 Jordan Lee: We also expose a compatibility matrix — what quant formats a model supports, recommended hardware (A100, H100, T4), and kernel maturity.
03:30 Priya Raman: Example, some of the newer open models are H100-optimized with certain kernels; for older community builds we may recommend different execution paths. We keep a 'compatibility score' per model and per runtime.
03:50 Liam O'Connor: How do rollouts work if we want to test a new quantized variant? Can we A/B between int8 and fp16?
04:02 Priya Raman: Yes — in the Console you can create routes and rollouts, canary a model variant, and automatic fallback to a hosted variant if Dedicated capacity is constrained.
04:18 Aisha Khan: What about determinism and reproducibility? We need consistent logits for evals.
04:25 Priya Raman: There's known non-determinism across quant levels; Redwood will capture per-run seeds, and we recommend keeping eval sets and using our quality monitoring to detect regressions.
04:45 Sofia Martinez: Security questions — bring your own KMS, HSM, SAML/SSO support?
04:52 Jordan Lee: Yes, BYOK via external KMS, HSM options on Private, full SAML SSO, RBAC, and per-token logging in the Console. We'll send the security appendix.
05:10 Priya Raman: Back to the catalog, here's a benchmark heatmap — you can sort by latency/cost/quality tradeoffs. See these rows: Llama-based forks, Mistral derivatives, and some family we label 'Redwood-verified'.
05:35 Liam O'Connor: Do you also include evals for hallucination or instruction-following?
05:40 Priya Raman: We include standardized evals and can attach customer prompt sets. Optimize supports alerting on quality regressions vs your baseline.
06:00 Jordan Lee: Objection we see often — "we already use X provider, why Redwood?" Any short pitch?
06:08 Priya Raman: Redwood is about serving consistency and economics: one API for hosted/dedicated/private, deterministic rollout controls, and observability to track per-route cost and latency.
06:25 Sofia Martinez: For our POC we'd want a small pilot: two routes (chat and embeddings), one model each, and run benchmarks end-to-end with our latencies.
06:34 Jordan Lee: Sounds good, recommended POC: 2-week pilot, Dedicated staging pool, run your eval set vs our benchmarks, implement canary rollouts.
06:45 Aisha Khan: Any limits on model families/licenses? We need to avoid models with problematic clauses.
06:50 Priya Raman: Catalog filters by license and flags models with restrictive terms. We can provide a legal matrix.
07:05 Liam O'Connor: Is quantization automated? Can Redwood auto-quant and test variants?
07:12 Priya Raman: Optimize will recommend quant profiles and we offer conversion tooling; full automation needs SE assistance for edge cases.
07:30 Jordan Lee: We'll also include expected costs for the pilot in the email.
07:35 Sofia Martinez: Perfect. A few nitty gritty questions — do you support on-prem air-gap?
07:42 Jordan Lee: Yes, Private can be air-gapped with an on-prem bundle; some features like hosted analytics will be limited.
07:55 Aisha Khan: For telemetry retention, what's the retention window and can we export logs?
08:02 Priya Raman: Default retention 90 days for observability; export via S3 or streaming to your SIEM; can increase retention for enterprise add-on.
08:20 Liam O'Connor: What about GPU mapping — we use GCP A2 (A100), we sometimes use H100 in other projects.
08:28 Priya Raman: We map runtime kernels by hardware. Some kernels are H100-optimized; our compatibility matrix flags performance deltas.
08:40 Sofia Martinez: This is super helpful. Let's talk concrete next steps.
08:46 Jordan Lee: Next steps — I'll send pricing+benchmarks, Priya will share POC template and compatibility matrix, and we schedule scoping next week.
09:00 Sofia Martinez: Thanks everyone.
09:05 End of recording.

Notes: Occasionally transcript mislabels speakers and auto-substitutes product names (e.g., 'kv cache'->'kayvee cache', 'Dedicated'->'de-dicated'). Shared artifacts: https://redwood.ai/model-catalog-demo-deck (demo deck), https://redwood.ai/security/soc2.pdf (security), https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/marisol-pilot.xlsx (benchmark sheet placeholder).
